result.topic_en: A short pencil calculation of the area of a triangle via Heron's formula in the form $16\Delta^2=-a^4-b^4-c^4+2a^2b^2+2b^2c^2+2a^2c^2$, applied to a triangle whose squared sides are sums of squares of three mutually perpendicular edges $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ (the face of a trirectangular tetrahedron).

methods.what: Heron's formula for the squared area of a triangle in terms of its side lengths
Rewriting Heron's formula as a difference of squares
Expressing the squared sides of a face through three mutually perpendicular edges (Pythagoras)
Area of the oblique face of a trirectangular tetrahedron (de Gua's theorem): $\Delta^2$ equals the sum of the squared areas of the three right-angled faces
